maintainer_decisions: Four steps, one phase, split by stack and then by file. The 16 scenarios partition cleanly: 1-3 backend write side, 4-6 backend read side, 7-10 the frontend boundary model, 11-16 the chart. Step-to-production-file ratio is 4 steps / 5 production files = 0.8, well inside the <= 2.5 guideline. Each step ends with its own named scenarios green and can be verified in isolation.

BACKEND FIRST, and not merely by convention. 02-04's chart scenarios consume the `totalItems` field shape 02-01 defines, and 02-03's `likelihood: number | null` is the consumer half of the producer widening made in 02-02 — reversing the order would mean the frontend tolerating a null the backend still 500s on. Within the backend, 02-01 (write) precedes 02-02 (read) so that the round-trip 02-02 proves is a round-trip of data 02-01 actually writes.

The nullable-likelihood repair is split ACROSS its two steps rather than gathered into one cross-stack step. The brief offered 'the nullable repair across both stacks' as one seam; it was rejected because its frontend half lands in the exact six lines of `parseFeatureBreakdown` that 02-03 rewrites anyway, and touching those six lines in two different steps buys nothing. The seam taken keeps each step inside one stack, one build, one test command — and honours CLAUDE.md's shared-contract rule by making 02-02 (the producer) strictly precede 02-03 (the consumer).

ESCALATION — 02-01 breaks two pre-existing tests, and 'zero changes to any test file' is not satisfiable as briefed. `DeliveryMetricSnapshotRecordingHandlerTest.cs:278` and `:347` assert `Assert.That(breakdown, Is.EquivalentTo(fixture.ExpectedBreakdown))`, where both sides are `DeliveryFeatureMetric` RECORDS. C# compiler-generated record equality covers the init-only `TotalItems` / `IsUsingDefaultSize` the DISTILL scaffold added, so the moment `ToFeatureMetric` populates them the deserialised entries (TotalItems 10 and 5, IsUsingDefaultSize false) stop equalling the fixture's (both null) and two currently-green tests go red. Recommended resolution: update the fixture at `:631-632` to `new DeliveryFeatureMetric("FEAT-1", "In Progress Feature", 40.0, CertainSingleBucketLikelihood) { TotalItems = 10, IsUsingDefaultSize = false }` and the FEAT-2 twin with `TotalItems = 5`. That is an expectation genuinely superseded by the widened contract, not an assertion weakened to fit the code, and the file is a pre-existing recorder test — NOT one of the four DISTILL-owned acceptance files. It still needs explicit maintainer sign-off before 02-01 is executed, because the rule as written says 'any test file'.

ESCALATION — 02-03 must change `FeverTrail.ts`, and DISTILL specifies no behaviour for it. `FeverTrail.ts:53` (`chanceOfLate: clamp(100 - metric.likelihood, 0, 100)`) is the ONLY consumer of `FeatureMetric.likelihood` in the whole frontend; widening the field to `number | null` breaks `tsc` there and forces a semantic choice — does an un-forecastable feature plot at maximum risk, or not plot at all? No scenario pins it and 02-03 may not author one. The step implements the narrowest total function (filter un-forecastable entries out of `dated` BEFORE grouping, so `latest` stays well-defined and `empty` stays correct) and flags the choice. If the maintainer wants it pinned, that is a DISTILL round-trip, not a crafter decision.

GAP — AC-2.6's legend half is uncovered. The AC reads 'remains listed in the legend (D7)', but `DeliveryEpicSizeChart.tsx` renders no `<ChartsLegend />` at all today and scenario 14 asserts only that EPIC-B's series values are `[3, 3, null]`. Keeping the series is necessary for the legend entry but not sufficient. 02-04 ships `<ChartsLegend />` as production behaviour verified at the dogfood moment rather than by a green assertion, and records it here so it is a known gap rather than a silent one. Note the slice-01 review already carried 'collapse the legend by default' to slice 04 — a per-epic legend will make this card tall.

NO test-authoring step. DISTILL authored all 16 scenarios and ran the fail-for-the-right-reason gate. Per ADR-025 / the slim-crafter scope, DELIVER implements against tests it does not own. Any step that adds, edits, widens or weakens an assertion in the four acceptance files is out of contract — if a test looks wrong, STOP and raise it, do not adjust it. This is distinct from the 02-01 fixture escalation above, which concerns a pre-existing test whose expectation the contract change supersedes.

Interim red is accepted and bounded, exactly as in slice 01. The backend suite is red after 02-01 (scenario 6 is 02-02's) and the frontend suite is red until 02-04. Per the project's green-before-push rule: commit at every step, push once at the end of 02-04. Do NOT push between 02-02 and 02-03 in particular — that window is the one where the backend has stopped 500-ing on a null likelihood and the frontend is still throwing `BoundaryError` on it. steps.description:
BEFORE WRITING ANY CODE, settle the escalation. `DeliveryMetricSnapshotRecordingHandlerTest.cs:278` and `:347` assert `Assert.That(breakdown, Is.EquivalentTo(fixture.ExpectedBreakdown))` where both sides are `DeliveryFeatureMetric` records, and C# record equality covers the init-only `TotalItems` / `IsUsingDefaultSize` the DISTILL scaffold added. The moment this step populates them, those two currently-green tests go red. The recommended resolution is a two-line fixture update at `:631-632` — `new DeliveryFeatureMetric("FEAT-1", "In Progress Feature", 40.0, CertainSingleBucketLikelihood) { TotalItems = 10, IsUsingDefaultSize = false }` and the FEAT-2 twin with `TotalItems = 5` (the fixture seeds `Feature([(team, 6, 10)])` and `Feature([(team, 0, 5)])`, so 10 and 5 are the honest totals and neither feature sets `IsUsingDefaultFeatureSize`, which defaults to false at `Feature.cs:45`). Get explicit maintainer sign-off first: the brief says zero changes to ANY test file, and this is the one place that cannot hold.

Then the production change, which is small. `Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/Models/Delivery.cs:152-159`, `ToFeatureMetric` — it already computes `var totalItems = feature.FeatureWork.Sum(work => work.TotalWorkItems)` on line 154 and then throws the number away. Stop discarding it: set `TotalItems = totalItems` and `IsUsingDefaultSize = feature.IsUsingDefaultFeatureSize` on the returned record via the init-only properties. Do NOT convert them to positional parameters — DISTILL rejected that explicitly, because two extra positional params would ripple through every construction site.

Note what this does NOT require: `CalculateFeatureBreakdown` at `:144-150` already filters out features with zero total items, so `TotalItems` is never zero on a recorded entry and the division at `:156` is already guarded. The recorder handler needs no change at all — it serialises `metrics.FeatureBreakdown` wholesale at `DeliveryMetricSnapshotRecordingHandler.cs:61-63`.

Then seed the demo instance. `Services/Implementation/DemoDataService.cs:195-214`: `BuildFeatureBreakdownJson` builds three anonymous feature metrics per elapsed day via `BuildFeatureMetric`, which currently emits only ReferenceId / Name / Completion / Likelihood. Add `TotalItems` and `IsUsingDefaultSize` to that shape and feed them per elapsed day. Two properties the seed must have, so the demo shows something worth looking at: the three epics' `TotalItems` should sum to that day's `BurnupTotalWorkByElapsedDay[elapsedDays]` (`:26` — 60 rising to 102, with a step up at day 5 and a dip at day 9), so the stacked bar tops out where the burnup's total line sits; and at least one epic must FLIP `IsUsingDefaultSize` from true to false on a specific day, with at least one other epic broken down throughout, so the estimate→actual transition slice 03 renders is already in the data. The day-9 dip from 98 to 86 reads naturally as 'an epic got broken down and turned out smaller' — a good day to hang the flip on. Exact arithmetic is the crafter's; those two properties are not.

steps.implementation_notes:
RECORD EQUALITY IS THE TRAP IN THIS STEP, and it is invisible until the suite runs. `DeliveryFeatureMetric` is a `sealed record`; the compiler-generated `Equals` covers init-only properties declared in the body exactly as it covers positional parameters. `Is.EquivalentTo` uses the default equality comparer, so it compares all six members. Nothing in the source reads as if it depends on the two new fields — the coupling is entirely in the generated equality. This is also worth carrying forward: any future field added to that record re-arms the same trap.

The demo seed is covered by NO acceptance scenario. It is verified by looking at the demo instance, not by a green test — which is the correct grain (it is sample data, not behaviour), but it does mean a silent mistake there survives the whole suite. Check it visually before calling the step done.

CI learnings apply (docs/ci-learnings.md — read it before writing, per CLAUDE.md, and pre-apply its rules rather than discovering them in CI). The backend rules that bite hardest on this kind of change are the INFO-severity ones `dotnet build` does not report: CA1859 (a member going public→private brings it into scope), CA1861 (inline `new[]` in an assertion), NUnit1028 (a non-`[Test]` fixture member left public), NUnit2046 (`Assert.That(collection.Count, ...)` instead of `Has.Count.EqualTo`), NUnit4002 (`Is.EqualTo(0)` instead of `Is.Zero`), NUnit2056 (`Assert.Multiple` instead of `using (Assert.EnterMultipleScope())`). One local run of the `dotnet format analyzers` command lists them all at once, before the first push; the per-pattern grep hook is not a substitute and has been observed to miss CA1861 twice.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: this step authors no tests at all — DISTILL owns the acceptance suite and DELIVER's slim-crafter scope forbids widening it — so the Hypothesis/state-delta unit mandate has no surface to apply to. The compensating rigour is DISTILL's own coverage: three scenarios over AC-2.1, AC-2.7 and AC-3.1, driven through `Delivery.CalculateMetrics` (the real aggregate entry point, not the private method), plus a passed fail-for-the-right-reason gate.

steps.name: A feature nobody can forecast stops taking the whole delivery's history down with it
steps.description:
The ADR-120 / DDD-6 repair, backend half. One line of production code and a comment; the value is entirely in knowing which line.

`Lighthouse.Backend/Lighthouse.Backend/API/DTO/DeliveryMetricsHistoryDto.cs:8` — widen `DeliveryFeatureMetricDto`'s `Likelihood` from `double` to `double?`. That is the whole fix.

Why it is a fix and not a preference: `DeliveryFeatureMetric.Likelihood` is `double?` because ADR-112 says an un-forecastable feature reports UNKNOWN — `Feature.GetLikelhoodForDate` returns null at `Feature.cs:114-122`. The recorder serialises the domain record verbatim (`DeliveryMetricSnapshotRecordingHandler.cs:61-63`), so `"Likelihood": null` reaches `FeatureBreakdownJson`. `ParseFeatureBreakdown` (`:72-80`) deserialises straight into the DTO, and System.Text.Json throws `JsonException` on null → double. One un-forecastable feature therefore 500s the ENTIRE delivery's metrics-history — every day, every other epic, the whole tab. Reachable whenever a delivery contains a feature with remaining work whose contributing team has no throughput. Not introduced by 5585; repaired here because this is the read path the slice widens. DESIGN inferred this from the type signatures; the DISTILL gate OBSERVED it (`System.Text.Json.JsonException: The JSON value could not be converted to DeliveryFeatureMetricDto. Path: $[0].likelihood`).

Check the blast radius before editing, per CLAUDE.md's shared-contract rule. `DeliveryFeatureMetricDto` has exactly two references outside its own declaration: `DeliveryMetricsHistoryPointDto.FeatureBreakdown` (`:25`) and `ParseFeatureBreakdown` (`:72-80`). The integration test at `DeliveryMetricsHistoryReadApiIntegrationTest.cs:715` deserialises into its OWN local `FeatureBreakdownView` record and is unaffected — leave it alone. On the wire the change is additive in the only direction that matters: a non-null likelihood serialises identically, and a null one now serialises as `null` instead of 500-ing.

Note what this step does NOT do: it does not make the FRONTEND tolerate that null. `asNumber` still throws `BoundaryError` on it. That is 02-03's half, and it is the reason this pair must not be pushed apart.

Also confirm — do not assume — that scenarios 4 and 5 (`From_ReadsTheSizeAndEstimateFlagRecordedForEachFeature`, `From_StillReadsASnapshotRecordedBeforeSizesWereEverWritten`) are still green. They went green off the DISTILL scaffold, which means nothing in this step should move them, which means a change in their status is a signal worth stopping for.

steps.implementation_notes:
The scenario asserts `Throws.Nothing`, NOT `Likelihood Is.Null`, and that is deliberate — do not read it as a weak test and do not try to strengthen it. DISTILL first wrote `Assert.That(dto…Likelihood, Is.Null)` and it would not COMPILE: `NUnit2023: the type of the actual argument 'double' can never be null`. The analyzer proves the mismatch statically, but a compile error is BROKEN, not RED, and a broken test proves nothing about the defect. `Throws.Nothing` is also the truer statement of the acceptance criterion: reading the delivery's history must not blow up.

A consequence worth naming: once `Likelihood` is `double?`, that NUnit2023 compile error disappears, so an `Is.Null` assertion would now compile. Do not add one — the test file is DISTILL's.

The comment already in the test file (`DeliveryMetricsHistoryDtoTest.cs:145-155`) carries the full rationale. Per CLAUDE.md's sparse-comments rule, the production comment on the widened property should be one line pointing at ADR-120 / ADR-112, not a restatement of it.

steps.name: The frontend boundary reads an epic's size, its estimate flag, and an unknown likelihood
steps.description:
`Lighthouse.Frontend/src/models/Delivery/DeliveryMetricsHistory.ts`, `parseFeatureBreakdown` at `:99-117`. Three changes in one function plus one interface, and one forced change in the single downstream consumer.

(1) DELETE the `// __SCAFFOLD__` marker and the two hard-coded `null`s at `:113-115`, and read both fields off the payload instead: `totalItems: asNullableNumber(metric.totalItems, "featureBreakdown.totalItems")` and an `asNullableBoolean` equivalent for `isUsingDefaultSize`. `asNullableNumber` already exists at `:50-55`; there is no nullable-boolean helper yet, so add one in the same shape as its siblings (return null for null AND undefined; throw `BoundaryError` naming the field for anything that is not a boolean). AC-3.5 is the load-bearing one here: a MISSING `isUsingDefaultSize` must parse as `null`, never as `false` — absence is not a guess, and if it parses as false then every pre-slice epic renders solid-by-assertion rather than solid-by-ignorance once slice 03 lands.

(2) Widen `FeatureMetric.likelihood` from `number` to `number | null` at `:10`, and change `:112` from `asNumber` to `asNullableNumber`, keeping the same context string. This is the frontend half of ADR-120 / DDD-6 — the backend can now emit `"likelihood": null` (02-02) and `asNumber` currently throws `BoundaryError` on it, which kills the whole tab rather than one epic. The gate captured it verbatim: `BoundaryError: Expected a number for featureBreakdown.likelihood`.

(3) The forced consumer change. `FeverTrail.ts:53` (`chanceOfLate: clamp(100 - metric.likelihood, 0, 100)`) is the ONLY reader of `FeatureMetric.likelihood` in the entire frontend — grep confirms one hit outside the model and its test. Widening the field breaks `tsc` there, and NO DISTILL scenario says what the fever chart should do with an un-forecastable feature. Implement the narrowest total function: filter entries whose `metric.likelihood === null` out of `dated` (`:39-41`) BEFORE deriving `referenceIds`, so a feature with no forecastable day never produces a series at all. Filtering downstream instead would leave a series with an empty `points` array and an `undefined` `latest`, which `DeliveryFeverChart` reads — that is a crash, not a degradation. Then FLAG the choice to the maintainer: it is a behaviour decision with no covering scenario, and if it should be pinned that is a DISTILL round-trip, not a crafter decision.

Run `pnpm vitest run src/models/Delivery/DeliveryMetricsHistory.test.ts src/models/Delivery/FeverTrail.test.ts` and expect all four breakdown scenarios green with `FeverTrail`'s existing suite untouched and still green.
criteria: All 4 scenarios in the `parseDeliveryMetricsHistory feature breakdown` describe pass, with no edit to DeliveryMetricsHistory.test.ts (`git diff --name-only` must not list it)
AC-2.4 — an entry recorded with `totalItems: 8` and `isUsingDefaultSize: true` parses as 8 and true
AC-2.4 — a four-field entry recorded before this slice parses with `totalItems` null and `isUsingDefaultSize` null, and raises no `BoundaryError`
ADR-120 / DDD-6 — an entry with `likelihood: null` parses with `likelihood` null instead of throwing
AC-3.5 — an entry carrying `totalItems` but NO `isUsingDefaultSize` parses the flag as `null`, never as `false`
The `// __SCAFFOLD__` marker is gone from `parseFeatureBreakdown`

The two new fields are read through nullable helpers that name the offending field in the error, matching the file's existing convention — a non-boolean `isUsingDefaultSize` and a non-numeric `totalItems` each raise a named `BoundaryError`

`FeverTrail.ts` compiles against the widened type and its existing suite is green with no edit to `FeverTrail.test.ts`; the null-likelihood behaviour chosen there is FLAGGED to the maintainer, not silently adopted
The other 24 pre-existing scenarios in DeliveryMetricsHistory.test.ts stay green — no collateral damage to the boundary-rejection or nullable-forward-field describes
`pnpm build` completes with zero errors and zero warnings (its `prebuild` hook implies a clean Biome check on ./src)
No new SonarQube issue of any severity — watch `typescript:S7735` (a negated condition in a ternary), which the nullable helpers' shape invites
The chart scenarios are still red at the end of this step — expected, they are 02-04's; commit, do NOT push

Lighthouse.Frontend/src/models/Delivery/FeverTrail.ts (:39-53 — the only consumer of FeatureMetric.likelihood, forced by the widening; ESCALATION, see description)
steps.implementation_notes:
TWO OF THESE FOUR SCENARIOS ARE ALREADY GREEN off the scaffold — 'still reads an epic recorded before sizes were ever written' and 'treats a missing estimate flag as unknown'. They pass today because the scaffold hard-codes both fields to null. That makes them a trap of a specific kind: they will KEEP passing if the new parsing is wrong in the direction of always-null, and only the other two scenarios distinguish a real read from the scaffold. Do not treat 4/4 green as proof on its own; confirm the two new fields actually come off the payload.

CLAUDE.md's shared-contract rule applies squarely here: `FeatureMetric` is a cross-cutting model. The grep was done and the answer is narrow — one consumer, `FeverTrail.ts:53`. That is the whole blast radius on the frontend. Do not widen the search into `likelihoodPercentage`, which is a different (snapshot-level) field that has been `number | null` for a long time.

The `FeverTrail` decision deserves stating plainly rather than being buried in a diff: before this slice, a null likelihood killed the entire metrics tab at the boundary, so the fever chart never saw one. After it, the fever chart sees a feature it cannot place on the risk axis, and 'not placed' is a better answer than 'placed at maximum risk' — a guess at 100% chance-of-late is indistinguishable from a measured 100%, which is exactly the confusion AC-3.5 exists to prevent in the sibling case. That reasoning belongs in the commit body, not in a comment (CLAUDE.md: comments are sparse, one line pointing at ADR-120 at most).

steps.name: Each day gains a stacked bar, one segment per epic, sized by its items
steps.description:
`Lighthouse.Frontend/src/components/Common/Charts/DeliveryEpicSizeChart.tsx`. Slice 01 shipped this component with the count line only and DDD-8 reserved the bars for exactly this step; the container, the card shell, the empty state, the x-axis and the tooltip are all already there and stay as they are. This step is additive.

Build the per-epic series from the history. Take every `referenceId` appearing in any day's `featureBreakdown` whose entry carries a non-null `totalItems`, de-duplicate, and SORT — the sort is not cosmetic. Membership changes day to day, and without a pinned order the same epic lands in a different band of the stack on consecutive days and the chart reads as noise (DESIGN OQ-4, scenario 16). Sort with `localeCompare` to match `getColorMapForKeys`'s own ordering exactly, so a series' stack position and its colour index agree.

Extend the dataset rows, one per recorded day, keeping slice 01's `label` and `epicCount` keys untouched. Each row gains one key per epic whose value is that epic's `totalItems` on that day, or `null` if the epic was absent or carried no size that day. `null` is load-bearing, not a shortcut: scenario 14 asserts `[3, 3, null]` for an epic present on days 1-2 and gone on day 3 — the segments STOP, they do not disappear retroactively, which is how a scope cut stays visible (D7). MUI's `DatasetType` is `Record<string, unknown>[]`, so a null value is well-typed and renders as no bar for that day.

Add one bar series per epic: `id` is the epic's `referenceId` (scenario 11 and 16 both address series by it), `type: "bar"`, `dataKey` the matching dataset key, `label` the epic's name (this is what the tooltip and the legend read), `yAxisId: "items"`, `stack` a single shared truthy value for every bar series (scenario 12 asserts exactly one distinct stack), and `color` from `getColorMapForKeys(sortedReferenceIds)` — `utils/theme/colors.ts:303`, default sorted mode, already the convention in four other charts (DDD-3). Colour must be stable per epic across days and across the slice-04 legend filter, which is what sorted mode buys.

Declare the `items` y-axis at `position: "left"`, alongside slice 01's `count` axis at `position: "right"` (ADR-122, scenario 15). Declare it ONLY when at least one bar series exists — DISTILL's resolved OQ-1 in slice 01 was that an axis with no series is a rendering risk for no gain, and a history recorded entirely before this slice has no bars. Scenario 13 covers exactly that case: seven legacy epics, zero bar series, and the count line still renders.

Render `<BarPlot />` BEFORE `<LinePlot />` so the count line draws on top of the bars, add `<ChartsYAxis axisId="items" />`, and add `<ChartsLegend />` so a segment is identifiable as a named epic — AC-2.6's 'remains listed in the legend' has no covering scenario (see maintainer_decisions) and is verified at the dogfood moment. Widen the left margin: it was 20 with no left axis and will clip the items scale.

Then the dogfood moment. Trigger a portfolio forecast update on the dogfood instance so one new snapshot day is recorded, open that delivery's Metrics tab, and confirm a single day's stacked bar appears with the count line unchanged over the older days. One day is expected, not a defect — the series only gets interesting as days accrue (forward-only, D11). Check the legend is readable and note (do not fix) how tall it makes the card; that is slice 04's business.
criteria: All 6 scenarios in the `DeliveryEpicSizeChart size bars` describe pass, with no edit to DeliveryEpicSizeChart.test.tsx (`git diff --name-only` must not list it)
AC-2.5 — a day with epics A:8 and B:3 produces exactly two bar series whose values on that day are 8 and 3
AC-2.5 — every bar series shares one single `stack` value, so the day's epics stack into one bar rather than standing side by side
AC-2.5 — a day whose entries carry no `totalItems` produces zero bar series and the count line still renders

AC-2.6 / D7 — an epic present on days 1-2 and absent on day 3 has dataset values `[3, 3, null]`: its segments stop, they do not vanish retroactively, and it keeps its series and therefore its legend entry
ADR-122 — the `items` axis is at `position: "left"`, every bar series carries `yAxisId: "items"`, and slice 01's `count` axis stays at `position: "right"` with the line series on it
DESIGN OQ-4 — bar series appear in sorted `referenceId` order regardless of the order epics appear in the day's breakdown, so bands do not reshuffle between days
DDD-3 — each epic's colour comes from `getColorMapForKeys` in sorted mode and is the same colour on every day it appears

All 10 slice-01 scenarios in the `DeliveryEpicSizeChart count line` describe stay green — the count line, its right-hand axis, the empty state, the terminology-driven title and the tooltip are untouched
No hatch, no `<pattern>`, no `slots.bar`, no estimate-flag tooltip wording, no `onItemClick` — slices 03 and 04
`pnpm test` passes in full — all 16 slice-02 scenarios plus the whole suite
`pnpm build` completes with zero errors and zero warnings (implies a clean Biome check on ./src via the prebuild hook)
No new SonarQube issue of any severity on the changed file
Dogfood moment done: forecast update triggered, one new snapshot day, a real stacked bar on the real instance with the count line intact over the older days
The whole slice is green on both stacks — only now push
steps.scenario_name: gives every epic on a day its own segment, sized by its items (AC-2.5) | stacks the day's epics into one bar rather than standing them side by side (AC-2.5) | draws no bar for a day recorded before sizes were written (AC-2.5, already green — must stay green) | keeps an epic that left the delivery on the days it was there (AC-2.6 / D7) | sizes the bars on their own left-hand scale, apart from the count (ADR-122) | orders the stack by epic so the bars do not reshuffle between days (DESIGN OQ-4)
files_to_modify: Lighthouse.Frontend/src/components/Common/Charts/DeliveryEpicSizeChart.tsx (add per-epic stacked bar series, the left items axis, BarPlot, ChartsLegend)
steps.implementation_notes:
MOCK-SURFACE COUPLING — slice 01 hit this and it must not be rediscovered. The test mocks `@mui/x-charts` with exactly EIGHT named exports (DeliveryEpicSizeChart.test.tsx:23-33): ChartsContainer, BarPlot, LinePlot, MarkPlot, ChartsXAxis, ChartsYAxis, ChartsTooltip, ChartsLegend. Importing a NINTH name from that barrel — ChartsGrid, ChartsAxisHighlight, ChartsSurface, BarLabel — resolves to `undefined` and React throws on render, breaking every scenario in the file at once. Importing from a deep path (`@mui/x-charts/BarChart`) bypasses the mock entirely and drags the real charting engine into jsdom. Import ONLY from the `@mui/x-charts` barrel and ONLY from those eight names. `BarPlot` and `ChartsLegend` are both on the list, which is exactly why this step can use them.

SCENARIO 13 IS ALREADY GREEN, and for the wrong reason — there are no bar series in the component at all yet, so 'zero bar series for a legacy day' passes trivially. It only becomes a real assertion once bar series exist. Treat a regression there as the signal that the non-null `totalItems` filter is missing, not as noise.

SINGLE-LEAF TERMINOLOGY MATCH still binds from slice 01. Scenario 'names the chart after whatever this instance calls its epics' uses `screen.getByRole("heading")` and asserts the heading does NOT contain /Epic/. Series labels are props on a mocked container and never reach the DOM, so epic NAMES in labels are safe — but do not add a second heading, an axis label, or a caption carrying the features term.

The count series is found by `id === "epic-count"` and the bar series by `type === "bar"`, so the position of the line within the `series` array is unconstrained by the tests. Its position among the CHILDREN is not: `<BarPlot />` before `<LinePlot />` determines SVG z-order in the real renderer, where the mock says nothing.

SCENARIO 14's `[3, 3, null]` requires the dataset row to carry an explicit `null`, not an absent key — an absent key reads as `undefined` and the assertion is `toEqual([3, 3, null])`. Build every row with every epic's key present.

The fixtures run through the REAL `parseDeliveryMetricsHistory`, which means this step inherits 02-03's work: `sizedEpic` in the test supplies `totalItems` but no `isUsingDefaultSize`, so the parser must already be returning the former and nulling the latter. If a bar scenario fails on a missing `totalItems`, the bug is in 02-03, not here.

CI learnings apply (docs/ci-learnings.md). Frontend-side, `typescript:S7735` (negated condition in a ternary) is the one this kind of null-handling code invites most.

EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: no tests are authored in this step. The compensating rigour is DISTILL's coverage of six scenarios over AC-2.5, AC-2.6 and ADR-122 plus the DESIGN open question, with fixtures built through the production boundary parser and every assertion made on the props handed to the container rather than on pixels — the repo-wide convention for all 30+ chart tests.
